title: Adversarial fuzz evals for quant regression + per-customer safety budgets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated adversarial-fuzz evaluation pipeline that exercises AWQ and GPTQ int4/int8 variants with amplified prompt sets and per-customer sensitivity budgets. The goal is to detect subtle semantic regressions introduced by quant config/model changes before rollout and to enforce per-customer fidelity budgets that can trigger automatic throttles or rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible fuzz harness runs on nightly and on-PR for quant-related changes and produces a summary report (pass/fail + delta metrics)
Setup per-customer sensitivity budgets in the eval platform and simulate budget consumption for at least 3 representative customers (low, mid, high tolerance)
Canary deployment pipeline integrates with dedicated-quant-canary pool and will auto-roll back a release if threshold breaches persist for two consecutive evaluation windows
Integration tests validate that fallback ladder (int4 -> int8 -> baseline fp16) triggers within configured TTL and does not exceed configured cost budget
Dashboard tiles in Console show top failing prompt families, embedding-drift deltas, and per-customer budget spend for the last 7 days
implementation_notes: Leverage existing eval harness but add: adversarial prompt mutator (synonym swaps, punctuation noise, length amplification), paraphrase generator, and intent-preserving perturbations.
Measure semantic drift using a stable embedding model (embed-v1-redwood) and compute per-prompt cosine delta distributions rather than only token-level metrics.

Define sensitivity budget as a rolling delta budget: customers have X allowable aggregate cosine-delta units per week per route; budgets consumptions are simulated in the nightly run to surface high-risk customers.
Add lightweight GPU microbenchmarks to ensure fuzzing workload doesn't saturate canary pool; schedule fuzz runs with staggered concurrency windows.

Implement a TTL-based rollback policy: if a quant variant exceeds thresholds for 30m across >5% of sampled prompts for a customer segment, trigger a throttle; sustained breach for 4 hours triggers automated rollback to fallback variant.
test_plan: Unit tests for adversarial mutator edge cases (preserve label, preserve core intent)
Simulated customer runs: run harness with three customer profiles and verify budget accounting and triggers
E2E on dedicated-quant-canary pool: deploy quant change, run fuzz suite, assert rollback behavior and that telemetry emitted to Console matches expectations
Chaos test: inject transient model-serving errors while fuzzing to verify rollbacks and retries do not loop indefinitely
artifacts: Dashboard: Console > Evals > Quant Fuzz Canary (work-in-progress)
risks: False positives from adversarial mutations could increase alert noise; need tuned thresholds and human review path.
Running fuzzing at scale can spike canary pool costs if not throttled; must add concurrency caps and off-peak scheduling.
Per-customer budgets risk exposing topology differences between customers; ensure synthetic customers map to real query distributions.
decisions: Use embed-v1-redwood as canonical semantic comparator to avoid metric drift when upstream embed models evolve.
Budget accounting will be additive and reset weekly; initial default budgets: low=0.05, mid=0.2, high=0.6 (cosine-delta-units/week)
Automated rollback TTL chosen = 4 hours for initial ramp; manual override allowed by SRE team via Console.
next_steps: Merge PR for adversarial mutator and run daily smoke jobs (assigned to Liam)
Create Console dashboard prototype and circulate to PM/design for feedback (Asha)
Schedule a cross-team review with SRE and Product to finalize budget defaults and rollback policies (owner: Asha)
Add canary pool rate-limiter to deployment pipeline to prevent fuzz jobs from preempting production bursts
